title: U.S. House · New York's 25th District
area: Monroe County, including the city of Rochester and surrounding suburbs.

context.text: Incumbent Joseph Morelle defeated Robin Wilt and Sherita Traywick in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary, 63.3%-30.6%-6.0%. The Republican and Conservative primaries were canceled; Virginia McIntyre advanced without appearing on either ballot.

summary.text: Joseph Morelle is the Democratic and Working Families Party incumbent, an Upstate New York native, former small-business owner and longtime local and state legislator. After serving on the Monroe County Legislature and in the New York State Assembly, where he was majority leader from 2013 to 2018, he won a 2018 special election to succeed the late Rep. Louise Slaughter. He is ranking member of the Committee on House Administration and serves on Appropriations.

background.text: Born in Oneida County, New York; his congressional biography describes him as a lifelong resident of Upstate New York.
Graduated from Eastridge High School and earned a bachelor's degree in political science from the State University of New York at Geneseo, graduating in 1986.
Worked as an administrator at the Anthony L. Jordan Health Center and as president and CEO of MMI Technologies, Incorporated; his congressional biography calls him a former small business owner.
Was previously elected to the Monroe County Legislature, according to his congressional biography.
Served in the New York State Assembly from 1991 to 2018, representing the 132nd District until 2013 and the 136th District from 2013 to 2018.
Was Assembly Majority Leader from 2013 to 2018.
Won the 2018 special election for New York's 25th District after the death of Rep. Louise Slaughter and has represented the district since.

Serves as ranking member of the Committee on House Administration and the Joint Committee on the Library and sits on the Appropriations Committee (Defense; Commerce, Justice, Science subcommittees) in the 119th Congress.
His office says he lives in Irondequoit with his wife, Mary Beth; they have three children and five grandchildren.

positions.summary: His official site says he supports measures to ban assault weapons, enact universal background checks and ban high-capacity magazines.
positions.quote: I’m proud to support numerous pieces of legislation to keep families safe from gun violence, including measures to ban assault weapons, enact universal background checks, ban the sale of high-capacity magazines, reduce gun theft and trafficking, and more.

positions.summary: His official site says he is fighting to enshrine the right to reproductive care in federal law.
positions.quote: That’s why I’m fighting to enshrine the right to reproductive care into federal law and continue to passionately advocate for women’s health freedom, pay equity, maternal care, and more.

positions.summary: In a May 2025 press release, he says he co-sponsored legislation to protect Medicaid from budget cuts and describes proposed Republican cuts as a threat to coverage.
positions.quote: This would have devastating consequences on seniors, children, and families who rely on these programs to receive basic healthcare and put food on the table. We must fight back against the Trump Administration’s repeated efforts to undermine the health and well-being of our community, which is why I’m proud to co-sponsor legislation to protect Medicaid and SNAP.

positions.summary: In a March 2026 statement as the top Democrat on the Committee on House Administration, he criticizes a Republican plan to advance the SAVE America Act through reconciliation as an attempt to make it harder for eligible Americans to vote.

record.text: Serves as ranking member of the House Committee on House Administration (Modernization and Innovation Subcommittee) and the Joint Committee on the Library, and sits on the House Committee on Appropriations (Defense; Commerce, Justice, Science and Related Agencies subcommittees) in the 119th Congress.

summary.text: Virginia McIntyre is a Monroe County Legislator from Gates who is the Republican and Conservative nominee. Her Ballotpedia survey describes a background as an educator, entrepreneur, international language professor and interpreter before she joined the county legislature in 2024. She says her campaign is built on fiscal accountability, public safety and government transparency.

background.text: Attended Gates Chili High School and earned an associate degree from Monroe Community College in 1998, a bachelor's degree from SUNY Purchase in 2001, and a bachelor's degree from the Conservatorio di Mantova in 2005.
Lists her career experience as educator, entrepreneur, international language professor and interpreter.
Has represented District 4 of the Monroe County Legislature, covering parts of Gates and Greece, since 2024.
Received the Monroe County Republican Committee's designation for the NY-25 race at its convention in February 2026 and launched her campaign at the Susan B. Anthony House in Rochester.
Ran unopposed for the Republican nomination, according to WHEC.
Is a Gates resident, according to WXXI.

priorities.text: Public safety, stronger local schools and expanding economic opportunity for working families.
Government accountability, transparency and fiscal responsibility, including tax relief for working families and seniors.
Says she has worked across party lines as a county legislator and will bring that approach to Congress.
priorities.quote: This campaign is about putting people over politics. I have worked across party lines to listen to constituents and act on their concerns, and I will bring that same approach to Washington.

positions.summary: As a Monroe County Legislator, voted no on adopting the county's Climate Action Plan Phase II.

record.text: Voted no on Resolution No. 231 of 2024, adopting the Monroe County Climate Action Plan Phase II, which passed the County Legislature 20-9 on August 13, 2024.

researchNotes: No campaign website was identified for Virginia McIntyre; her priorities and positions come from her 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, supplemented by one Monroe County Legislature floor vote (verified against the official minutes) on the county's Climate Action Plan. A broader search of 2024-2025 Monroe County Legislature minutes for other votes matching this guide's fixed issue statements did not turn up additional squarely-matching roll calls within the time available. Morelle has not completed a recent Candidate Connection survey and no current campaign-site issues page was accessible, so his priorities/positions are limited to what his official committee record documents. Federal key votes and FEC totals for incumbent Joseph Morelle are added separately by script. McIntyre's biography is limited to her Ballotpedia survey and local news; no campaign website, birthplace or non-legislative employer details could be found. Morelle's congressional biography gives no birth year or birthplace beyond Oneida County.
